newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Oppenheim still rates SMH as a "buy".
newsitem.headline: Oppenheim still rates SMH as a "buy".

text.p: Bank Sal Oppenheim & Cie, countering a recent negative report on Suisse Microelectronique et d'Horlogerie (SMH), reiterated its buy recommendation on the stock and said it expected the company's profit momentum to be maintained by its strong core watch business.

Oppenheim said in its report that SMH, creator of the Swatch brand, last week confirmed a positive pre-Christmas order trend showing growth for the first time in both the high-price and low-price watch segments. It said the Omega brand led the advance with sales growth of between 17 and 20 percent.
The bank forecast 1996 net profit growth for SMH of 37 percent, followed by 25.2 percent growth in 1997 and 10.3 percent in 1998.
Earlier this month Standard & Poor's Marketscope said it saw greater risks to SMH than generally recognised stemming from its Smart Car joint venture with Daimler-Benz AG.
The Smart car, developed by Daimler's Mercedes-Benz together with SMH, will be launched at prices of between 15,000 and 20,000 marks and is due to come onto the market in 1998.
The joint venture has projected annual sales at 200,000 by 2000. But Marketscope said the sales projection "may prove wildly optimistic".
Bank Sal. Oppenheim said in its report circulated on Friday that the car's developer maintains that profitability could be maintained at 100,000 units.
